metadata.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array II

problem_summary.summary: Compact a sorted integer array in place, allowing each value to appear no more than twice while preserving order.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: non-decreasing nums. Return k and store the allowed values in nums[0..k-1]; values beyond that prefix do not matter.
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order

brute_force.explanation: Scan the sorted input while counting each run, copy at most its first two values to a temporary array, then copy the kept prefix back.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Each value forms one contiguous run; limiting each run to two copies implements the required multiplicity while retaining the input order.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n) — one scan and one prefix copy.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary — a temporary array holds the compacted result.

optimized.explanation: Maintain a write length. A sorted value can be written if fewer than two values have been written or it differs from the value two positions behind the write pointer.
optimized.correctness_idea: The first two values are always allowed. Thereafter, matching nums[write - 2] would create a third copy, while differing from it keeps the new run count at no more than two.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — each element is tested once.
optimized.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary — only indices are used.

steps.action: Keep the first 1 at index 0; write becomes 1.
Keep the second 1 at index 1; write becomes 2.

steps.condition: nums[read] equals nums[write - 2], so accepting it would make a third copy.

steps.action: Write the second 2 at index 3; write becomes 4.
Write the second 3 at index 5; write becomes 6.

steps.condition: nums[7] equals nums[4], so it would be a third 3.

edge_cases.handling: Every value passes the initial write < 2 allowance.

edge_cases.case: A value appears once or twice

edge_cases.handling: Only its first two values enter the output prefix.
